summary: Fix run on martin/2026-10-close: the safety net exists (15 tests, about 17 s, offline, green twice in a row, red on mutations in a clone) and every approved finding is applied, including Next 16 (D1) and the shim move (D2), each checked against the content extract and the consent probe. npm audit went from 7 to 5, all in the linter's braces chain with no patched release; Tailwind 4.3.3 changes the served CSS and comes back as decision D4. Building the net found that Tailwind scanned tests/ and code-health/ for class names, which would have shipped stray CSS: both are now excluded and the CSS is byte-identical to production.

Offline build from a clean .next (fonts from fixtures over a local server, clock frozen, NODE_ENV production), byte goldens of 1659 files, per-page content extract, data goldens over 243 books, build-books.py byte golden, Playwright smoke with the consent probe. 0 critical, 0 moderate. 5 high remain, all in braces via fast-glob 3.3.1 inside @next/eslint-plugin-next 16.4.0: lint-time only and braces has no patched release (card). gitleaks 0; .gitignore now covers every .env file.

Next and eslint-config-next 16.4.0, react 19.3.0, types and eslint in range. Left: Tailwind 4.3.3 (changes the served CSS, decision D4), typescript 7 and @types/node 26 (kept out by Joseda). Python deps pinned in scripts/requirements.txt.

build-books.py main() CCN 44 split (top function now 16); one GA_ID; SECTIONS generated into src/data/sections.json; the shim no longer sits under <html> (no dev hydration error).
Runs once in the last repo of the monthly pass.

decisions.text: Upgrade to Next 16 now? Recommendation: yes, in today's fix run right after the safety net, as its own commit through 'approved output change'. Security gain at runtime is nil (residual vulns are build/lint only and 15.5 still gets backports), but it clears audit noise so the next real alert stands out, and the migration is small: params already async; `next lint` -> ESLint CLI (codemod), images.qualities [62, 75], flat eslint config. If approved: every page's framework markup changes, so the byte goldens are re-pinned and the semantic extract plus the Playwright smoke are the guard. TypeScript 7 and @types/node 26 stay out.
